clue.text: Unprofessional, and certainly not brave!

definitions.meaning: a ... builder or plumber is a slapdash, unqualified operator
in Westerns the ... fight the Indians, whose warriors are called braves

explanation.surface: Someone is scolded as amateurish and cowardly into the bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowboy is British slang for a shoddy tradesman, and in cowboys-and-Indians play a cowboy is the opposite of a Native American brave.

clue.text: A constant diet of dripping?

parts.note: dripping here is not beef fat but ... falling drop by drop on a victim's forehead, a famous slow torment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dripping' tempts you towards the British fat spread on toast; the diet is really an endless series of drops, an interrogation method.
explanation.definitionFit: This form of torment drips water steadily onto the head, so the victim gets a constant diet of drips.

clue.text: See 1
Person seen in mirror taking ecstasy's a pixie

parts.note: someone on drugs is taking them, so taking gives on
E is the drug ecstasy; with the possessive it gives E's
an elf is a small mischievous sprite like a pixie

explanation.surface: A drug-taker gazing into a mirror sees a pixie staring back.
explanation.definitionFit: When you look in a mirror the person you see is yourself, the reflexive form of 'one'.

clue.text: Run second photo

parts.note: a print is a photograph developed on paper

explanation.surface: An athlete's run is captured in a photo finish, second place.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprint is a short fast run, so the noun matches the noun run.

clue.text: Writer has to test his work?

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American author, is a stock crossword writer
to try is to test or attempt

explanation.surface: An author must put his output to the test.
explanation.definitionFit: Poe wrote verse such as The Raven, so his work includes poetry.

clue.text: Popular deception almost taking in partners, one appearing genuine

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: taking in means the shortened word swallows the other pieces
almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a trick is a deception
I is the Roman numeral one
N and S, North and South, are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A con trick that ropes in a couple seems authentic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partners' is bridge shorthand, North and South. 'almost' docks the deception's last letter to leave TRIC, and 'taking in' wraps that round the one and the partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrinsic means essential or inherent, belonging to a thing's true nature, so genuine in that sense.

clue.text: See 1
Targeted man died supporting front line, you might say?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Targeted man died supporting front line, you might say? (6,7)' for CENTRE FORWARD: no parse found that accounts for every word; CENTRED for 'Targeted' and D for 'died' clash, and no source gives the setter's parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Targeted man died supporting front line, you might say?

clue.text: See 16
Simple people in Lear, yet nonsensical

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other
nonsensical suggests the letters are jumbled, and nods to Edward Lear the nonsense poet

parts.note: men are people

explanation.surface: Something simple about folk in Edward Lear's verse, yet it makes no sense.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invokes Edward Lear, the nonsense poet, so 'nonsensical' doubles as a fitting anagram signal, giving ELETARY; 'in' then sets the people inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary means basic or simple, as in elementary arithmetic.

clue.text: Extent requiring qualification

definitions.meaning: a university ... is an academic qualification

explanation.surface: How far one gets depends on having the right certificate.
explanation.definitionFit: A degree is both an amount or extent and an academic award.

clue.text: Bird won't finish — end of journey

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Bird won't finish — end of journey (8)' for TERMINUS: the only reading is TERN minus its finish written as TER + MINUS, a whole-phrase reverse reading the check refuses; no source gives another parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Bird won't finish — end of journey

clue.text: See 17
Seven and ace, possibly diamonds, vanished

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A card player holds a seven and an ace of diamonds, and they disappear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges SEVEN ACE into EVANESCE, then D is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To evanesce is to fade from sight, so evanesced is a literary synonym for vanished.

clue.text: Separate land blocking entrance to passage

indicators.note: blocking entrance to means the first letter of the word is barred

parts.note: an aisle is a passage between seats

explanation.surface: An area of ground cuts off the way into a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, a piece of land separated from others by water.

clue.text: Black hole after dose of nuclear energy has little time for huge star

indicators.note: after puts the hole later in the answer than the dose

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a rad is a unit of absorbed radiation dose
a pit is a hole in the ground
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An astronomical description: a black hole forms after a nuclear burst and swallows a giant star in moments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'huge star' sounds astronomical but means a film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Brad Pitt is a Hollywood actor, a huge star of the screen.

clue.text: Shocker, with monarch allowed source of information

parts.note: boo is what you shout to give someone a fright
K is the abbreviation for king
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A scandalous tabloid tale about a king being allowed something is an information source.
explanation.definitionFit: A booklet is a small pamphlet that gives information.

clue.text: Awful hooey cute Monroe fed? She'll have heard it all before

definitions.text: She'll have heard it all before

indicators.note: awful suggests something mangled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Marilyn Monroe is fed awful cute nonsense by an admirer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges HOOEY CUTE MONROE FED into the four-word chat-up line.
explanation.definitionFit: This hackneyed pick-up line is one a woman will have heard countless times.

clue.text: Acting male one's screened

indicators.note: screened means the male is concealed inside the other word

parts.note: one gives one, its 's meaning has
a stag is a male deer

explanation.surface: A male actor appears in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'one's screened' as 'one has screened': ONE hides STAG, giving ON(STAG)E.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor on stage is performing, so on stage means acting.

clue.text: Doctor needed to loosen someone up in Canada?

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
to untie is to loosen a knot

explanation.surface: A medic is needed to relax a patient visiting the far north.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mountie is a member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, someone found up north in Canada.

clue.text: Buddy bites lip first

indicators.note: bites means one word holds the other in its mouth

parts.note: a pal is a buddy
a rim is a lip or edge

explanation.surface: A friend bites a lip before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Primal means original or earliest, so first in time.

clue.text: Drink order placed in ancient language

indicators.note: placed in means the order sits inside the language

parts.note: Hebrew is an ancient language
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone orders a drink in an old tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Home-brew is beer or wine made at home, a kind of drink.

clue.text: Star quaffing alcoholic drink — it's a slippery slope!

indicators.note: quaffing means drinking down, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: the sun is a star
kir is white wine with blackcurrant liqueur

explanation.surface: A celebrity drinking heavily is heading downhill fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski run is a snowy downhill track, literally a slippery slope.

clue.text: Nation in plan to lose weight

indicators.note: to lose means part of the word is dropped

parts.note: a diagram is a plan
a gram is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A country has a scheme for slimming down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose' takes GRAM from DIAGRAM, leaving DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a nation in South Asia.

clue.text: Prisoners transported by this card game?

definitions.meaning: a police van for carrying prisoners
a trick-taking card game where players avoid the queen of spades

explanation.surface: Convicts are carried off by playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Black Maria is old slang for a police van and also the name of a hearts-like card game.

clue.text: Fruitful rendezvous?

parts.note: read as a productive meeting, but it means an appointment that is also a fruit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruitful' seems to mean successful; it really says the meeting's name is also a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A date is both a romantic meeting and the sweet fruit of the palm.

clue.text: A little drunk, in order to drink 500 litres

indicators.note: to drink means one word swallows the others

parts.note: tidy means neat, in order
D is the Roman numeral 500

explanation.surface: Someone tidily downs a huge quantity and is a bit tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiddly is informal British for slightly tipsy.

clue.text: Waste picture, framing comic

indicators.note: framing means one word surrounds the other

parts.note: to picture is to see in the mind
a wag is a joker or comic

explanation.surface: A rubbish picture with a cartoon in its frame.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewage is waste matter carried away in sewers.
